definitions.explanation: The style or design of written characters, whether in calligraphy, printing, or digital fonts. Covers both traditional calligraphic styles and modern digital typefaces.

examples.japanese: この{書類|しょるい}にはどの{書体|しょたい}を{使|つか}いますか。
examples.english: Which typeface will you use for this document?

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{楷書|かいしょ}や{行書|ぎょうしょ}など、さまざまな{書体|しょたい}がある。
examples.english: Japanese has various script styles such as block script and semi-cursive.

notes:
{書体|しょたい} refers to the style or design of written characters, covering both traditional calligraphic styles and modern digital typefaces.

TRADITIONAL STYLES:
- {楷書|かいしょ}: block script (standard, clear strokes)
- {行書|ぎょうしょ}: semi-cursive script
- {草書|そうしょ}: cursive script

MODERN TYPEFACES:
- {明朝体|みんちょうたい}: Ming/serif typeface
- ゴシック{体|たい}: Gothic/sans-serif typeface

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書体|しょたい}を{選|えら}ぶ: to choose a typeface
- {書体|しょたい}を{変更|へんこう}する: to change the font
- {書体|しょたい}の{種類|しゅるい}: types of typefaces

SIMILAR WORDS:
The loanword フォント (font) is commonly used in digital contexts and is nearly interchangeable with {書体|しょたい} when referring to computer fonts.
